types.label: Prefix
types.rule: The perfective adds a prefix to the imperfective. This is the most common way to make a pair, and the prefix usually keeps a trace of its own meaning (na- = onto, done to completion).
types.note: A prefix can change the meaning as well as the aspect, so not every prefixed verb is a partner: pisać → podpisać is "to sign", not "to write".

types.label: Suffix
types.rule: The imperfective is made longer, with -ować, -ywać, -ać or -awać, and the perfective is the shorter word. This is the direction to remember: the longer verb is the one that repeats.
types.note: This is the largest group for the verbs that describe a single act: kupić/kupować, dać/dawać, zamknąć/zamykać.

types.label: Suppletive
types.rule: Two unrelated roots. There is no rule to apply — the pair has to be learnt whole, like an irregular verb in English.
types.note: Only a handful, but they are among the most used verbs in the language: brać/wziąć, mówić/powiedzieć, widzieć/zobaczyć.

types.label: One word, both readings
types.form: czytać (impf) — no perfective partner of its own
types.rule: A few imperfective verbs have no perfective partner at all, because their meaning does not allow completion in the ordinary sense: być, mieć, wiedzieć, znać, mieszkać.
types.note: Where you need "to finish doing it", Polish uses a prefixed verb with a slightly different meaning (przeczytać = to read through), not a partner of the same verb.

pairs.note: na- adds completion, not direction.
prze- = through: to read something through.
z- is the plainest completing prefix in the language.
Also powiadać, a bookish imperfective of powiedzieć.
zjeść = to eat up; jeść is the process.
wy- = out, to the end.
The short perfective is the older word; dawać is the lengthened imperfective.
No shared root at all.
kupować is the repeated or ongoing act; kupić, one purchase, done.
Same -awać / -ać pattern as dawać/dać.
-ać / -yć; the perfective has the -yć of a single completed act.
A different suffix again: -ykać / -knąć.
The perfective is a single starting point; the imperfective is the run-up.
s- here completes without adding direction.
zobaczyć is "to catch sight of", a different root from widzieć.
u- marks the single act of hearing something.
za- = the one ring that reaches someone.
po- softens and completes the request.
zapytać is one question; pytać is asking in general.
The -ać / -eć pattern, like czytać/przeczytać's cousins.
zrozumieć = to come to understand, and now you do.
Both keep się.
nauczyć kogoś czegoś — the person in the accusative, the thing in the genitive.
u- completes the feeling; both keep się.
pamiętać is the state; zapamiętać is the act of committing it to memory.
-ać / -eć again.
pójść is the one journey, started and completed; iść is the walking.
Same po- as pójść, for the same reason.
pobiec = to set off running.
wyspać się = to get one's sleep, to sleep it off; the się is part of the verb.
umyć ręce = to wash one's hands (and have them clean).
po- here means "for a while": popracować nad czymś.
zamieszkać = to move in, to take up residence.
The repeated, back-and-forth partner of jechać.
The repeated, back-and-forth partner of iść — and its perfective is pójść, not a prefixed chodzić.
stać = to be standing; stanąć = to take a stand, one act.
poleżeć = to lie for a while. The single act of lying down is położyć się.
posiedzieć = to sit for a while; the act of sitting down is usiąść.
